commits.message:
style(pretty): derive EXPAND_SEPARATOR from SEPARATOR instead of a second literal

Medium review: two independently hand-typed literals for the same
punctuation is exactly the drift risk EXPAND_SEPARATOR's own comment says
it exists to prevent.

refactor(pretty): tighten Frame allocation and column tracking from repeat high review

- _formatObject's per-slot Frame varied only in `reserve`, which takes just
  two values (last slot vs every other), so build two shared frames instead
  of one per slot — was O(N) allocations for an N-slot container, now O(1).
- _expandSlot tracked `column` as a second variable hand-synchronized with
  `out` at every append. Derive it instead via lineColumn(at.column, out) —
  one source of truth, and a future third piece of per-hole text can no
  longer update `out` without updating `column` to match, which would have
  silently reintroduced a stale-budget bug of the same shape this PR fixes.

A third finding — the expand branch's own opening-bracket line (`key: Set {`)
is emitted with no width check against `at.column` at all, unlike the
compact try a few lines above it — is real, pre-existing (confirmed
unaffected by every fix on this branch), and needs a different fix shape
(there's no way to reflow a fixed literal like `Set {`; the real fix is a
design decision about breaking the key onto its own line). Filed as
rich-pretty-xms.0l4 rather than folded into this PR.

fix(pretty): a container's compact try also charges for what follows it

The medium review on this PR found the same accounting gap on the trailing
side: a non-last slot's compact value can fit maxWidth - column exactly and
still overrun once _formatObject's own trailing "," lands after it, wrapping
mid-container the same way the leading-key bug did.

Frame gains `reserve`: cells a fixed piece of literal text already known to
follow a value — the rest of its own hole.tail, or the slot-join separator —
will cost on the same line, charged symmetrically with `column`. Threaded
through _expandSlot per hole (only the slot's last hole inherits the outer
slot's own reserve) and through _formatObject's per-slot Frame (0 for the
last slot, 1 for every other).

Verified the same gap exists, symmetrically, for a Map entry's " => " tail
following a compact key — fixed by the same mechanism, pinned by a second
test. A third manifestation (a bare scalar or self-describing value trailing
a compact key within one slot, e.g. `[1,2,3,10] => "v"`) shares the same root
cause but needs a different fix shape (scalars/self-describing text have no
compact-fit apparatus at all) — confirmed present on master already, not a
regression from either fix on this branch, and added to the already-filed
follow-up ticket (rich-pretty-xms.tmf) rather than fixed here.

fix(pretty): address high-review findings on rich-pretty-xms

- Hoist the per-slot `deeper` Frame back to a single construction outside
  `.map()` — every field was identical across slots at a given nesting
  level (column: innerColumn doesn't vary per slot, only _expandSlot's own
  running column varies per hole within one), so building it fresh per
  slot was pure allocation churn with no behavioral difference.
- The new width-pinning test compared raw `.length` instead of `cellLen`,
  diverging from every other width assertion in this file and from the
  budget math the fix itself is built on. Switched to `cellLen`.

A third finding (Pretty's self-describing "text" shape — Error, custom
toString — never consults column/width for multi-line values) is real but
pre-existing and out of this ticket's scope; filed as rich-pretty-xms.tmf.

fix(pretty): a container's compact try is charged for the key it sits under (rich-pretty-xms)

Pretty's fit-on-one-line decision for a nested container budgeted the
remaining width as maxWidth minus the indent alone, which is only the true
remaining width when nothing precedes the value on its line. A value under
a key — `metadata: { ... }` — has that key's width and separator eaten
from the same line, uncounted, so a container could pass the fit test and
still overrun the width once its key was prepended, wrapping mid-container.

Frame now carries `column`: where a value's text actually begins on the
line it lands on, threaded through `_expandSlot` per hole (so a Map
entry's `" => "` and a second hole are charged too, and a multi-line
insert resets the column to its own last line rather than accumulating
across lines that were never on the same row). The one-line probe path
already tracked this correctly via its shrinking `budget`; only the
lay-out path's own compact try was deriving the budget from depth instead
of position.

fix(docs): drop double-stacked newlines in group.md's Group examples (rich-flexstrip-5kf.c4u) (#147)

commit f1fa4c67 (rich-text-5ai) made RichText.render() draw its `end`
unconditionally. All three Group examples on docs/group.md built their
RichText/renderMarkup content with a literal trailing "\n" in the text
AND relied on the default end ("\n"), so every item printed a spurious
blank line after it. Drop the literal "\n"s and let the default `end`
supply the line break, matching what the page's shown output already
claims. Also corrects the explanatory paragraph, which asserted
`console.print` (not RichText itself) draws the default `end` -- true
before f1fa4c67, false since.
